subject: maths
title: Place Value to 1,000: Hundreds, Tens and Ones, 10 or 100 More or Less
seo_title: Year 3 Place Value Worksheets: Hundreds, Tens and Ones, Numbers to 1,000 in Words
standard_text: Count from 0 in multiples of 4, 8, 50 and 100; find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number; recognise the place value of each digit in a three-digit number (hundreds, tens, ones); compare and order numbers up to 1,000; identify, represent and estimate numbers using different representations; read and write numbers up to 1,000 in numerals and in words.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 place value maths worksheets for the National Curriculum: hundreds, tens and ones with base-ten blocks and place value counters, numbers to 1,000 in numerals and words, 10 or 100 more or less, counting in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s, and comparing and ordering. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A 3-digit number is hundreds, tens and ones. The place of a digit decides its value.
key_sub: The 4 in 349 is worth 40. Three hundred and six is 306: write 0 when there are no tens. For 10 more or less change the tens digit; for 100 more or less change the hundreds digit.
body_html:
Hundreds, tens and ones

A 3-digit number has a hundreds digit, a tens digit and a ones digit. The place tells you what the digit is worth. 10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred.

Numerals and words

NumeralWordsPartitioned
243two hundred and forty-three200 + 40 + 3
306three hundred and six300 + 6
415four hundred and fifteen400 + 10 + 5
750seven hundred and fifty700 + 50
1,000one thousand10 hundreds

Say “and” after the hundreds. Use a hyphen for numbers like forty-three.

Write in numerals

Write “three hundred and six” in numerals.

3 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones. Write 3, 0, 6.

Answer: 306 (not 3006 or 36)

10 or 100 more or less

For 10 more or less, change the tens digit. For 100 more or less, change the hundreds digit.

100 less10 lessNumber10 more100 more
247337347357447
195285295305395

Watch out at 9 tens: 295 + 10 = 305, because 10 tens make 1 hundred.

Counting in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s

Count inNumbers
4s4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40
8s8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80
50s50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400
100s100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700

The 8s are double the 4s. Counting in 50s always ends in 00 or 50.

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 3-digit number is greater than any 2-digit number. If both have 3 digits, compare the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Compare

419 ☐ 501

Hundreds: 4 < 5. You can stop here. The 9 ones do not matter.

Answer: 419 < 501

< means “is less than”. > means “is greater than”. The open side faces the bigger number.

Estimate on a number line

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing “three hundred and six” as 3006 or 36Use 3 digits with 0 tens: 306
Giving the digit, not its value (the 4 in 349 is 4)The 4 is in the tens place: 40
Changing the wrong digit (295 + 10 = 395)10 more changes the tens: 305
Comparing the last digits (419 > 501 because 9 > 1)Compare the hundreds first: 419 < 501
Mixing up fifteen and fifty (415 and 450)Fifteen is 1 ten, 5 ones: 415

faq.q: What place value should a Year 3 child know?
faq.a: Year 3 children work with numbers up to 1,000. They know the value of each digit in a 3-digit number, read and write numbers in numerals and words, find 10 or 100 more or less, count in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s, and compare and order numbers.

faq.q: How do you write numbers in words in Year 3?
faq.a: Say the hundreds, then “and”, then the tens and ones, for example 243 is two hundred and forty-three and 306 is three hundred and six. Numbers from 21 to 99 use a hyphen, like forty-three.

faq.q: How do you find 10 or 100 more or less than a number?
faq.a: For 10 more or less, change the tens digit by 1; for 100 more or less, change the hundreds digit by 1. Take care at 9 tens: 10 more than 295 is 305.

faq.q: Why does my child write 3006 for three hundred and six?
faq.a: They write each part they hear: 300 and then 6. Show that three hundred and six is 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones, so it has only 3 digits: 306.

items.e: A big square is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 hundreds, 7 tens and 1 one: 300 + 70 + 1 = 371.
A big square is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 5 hundreds, 4 tens and 2 ones: 500 + 40 + 2 = 542.
A big square is 1 hundred. A rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 one. Count each kind: 4 hundreds, 6 tens, 9 ones. The number is 469.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens = 80. The digit is 8, but its value is 80.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 4 hundreds = 400. The digit is 4, but its value is 400.
A big square is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones: 400 + 8 = 408. There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place.

items.q: What number do the place value counters show?
items.e: Count the counters in each box. 6 hundreds, 8 tens and 2 ones: 600 + 80 + 2 = 682.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 349?
items.e: The 4 is in the tens place, so it is worth 4 tens = 40. The digit is 4, but its value is 40.

items.q: In 276, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 276 has 2 hundreds, 7 tens, 6 ones. The tens digit is 7.
A big square is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 5 hundreds, 6 tens and 8 ones: 500 + 60 + 8 = 568.
A big square is 1 hundred. A rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 one. Count each kind: 4 hundreds, 3 tens, 2 ones. The number is 432.

items.q: What number do the place value counters show?
items.e: Count the counters in each box. 7 hundreds, 0 tens and 1 one: 700 + 1 = 701. There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the tens place, so it is worth 2 tens = 20. The digit is 2, but its value is 20.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 854?
items.e: The 8 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 8 hundreds = 800. The digit is 8, but its value is 800.
A big square is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 hundreds, 7 tens and 0 ones: 300 + 70 = 370. There are no ones, so write 0 in the ones place.

items.q: In 295, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 295 has 2 hundreds, 9 tens, 5 ones. The hundreds digit is 2.

items.q: What number do the place value counters show?
items.e: Count the counters in each box. 6 hundreds, 7 tens and 0 ones: 600 + 70 = 670. There are no ones, so write 0 in the ones place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 2 hundreds = 200. The digit is 2, but its value is 200.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A big square is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones: 200 + 7 = 207. There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 678?
items.e: The 7 is in the tens place, so it is worth 7 tens = 70. The digit is 7, but its value is 70.

sets.title: Read and write numbers to 1,000 in numerals and words

items.q: Write two hundred and three in numerals.
items.e: Two hundred and three means 2 hundreds, 0 tens, 3 ones: 200 + 3 = 203. Write 0 in the tens place. 3-digit numbers have only 3 digits, so it is not 2,003.

items.q: Write one hundred and seventy-eight in numerals.
items.e: One hundred and seventy-eight means 1 hundred, 7 tens, 8 ones: 100 + 70 + 8 = 178.

items.q: How do you write 136 in words?
items.e: 136 is 1 hundred, 3 tens, 6 ones. Say the hundreds, then “and”, then the tens and ones: one hundred and thirty-six.

items.q: How do you write 201 in words?
items.e: 201 is 2 hundreds, 0 tens, 1 one. Say the hundreds, then “and”, then the tens and ones: two hundred and one. There are 0 tens, so we say nothing for the tens.

items.q: What number is 400 + 7?
items.e: 400 + 7 is 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. Write 0 in the tens place: 407.

items.q: Write nine hundred and sixteen in numerals.
items.e: Nine hundred and sixteen means 9 hundreds, 1 ten, 6 ones: 900 + 10 + 6 = 916.

items.q: Which shows 704 partitioned into hundreds, tens and ones?
items.e: 704 has 7 hundreds, 0 tens, 4 ones. Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 700 + 4.

items.q: How do you write 815 in words?
items.e: 815 is 8 hundreds, 1 ten, 5 ones. Say the hundreds, then “and”, then the tens and ones: eight hundred and fifteen. 15 is “fifteen”, not “fifty”.

items.q: How do you write 380 in words?
items.e: 380 is 3 hundreds, 8 tens, 0 ones. Say the hundreds, then “and”, then the tens and ones: three hundred and eighty.

items.q: Write three hundred and one in numerals.
items.e: Three hundred and one means 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 1 one: 300 + 1 = 301. Write 0 in the tens place. 3-digit numbers have only 3 digits, so it is not 3,001.

items.q: What number is 600 + 30?
items.e: 600 + 30 is 6 hundreds, 3 tens and 0 ones. Write 0 in the ones place: 630.

items.q: How do you write 536 in words?
items.e: 536 is 5 hundreds, 3 tens, 6 ones. Say the hundreds, then “and”, then the tens and ones: five hundred and thirty-six.

items.q: Write two hundred and sixty in numerals.
items.e: Two hundred and sixty means 2 hundreds, 6 tens, 0 ones: 200 + 60 = 260. Write 0 in the ones place.

items.q: Which shows 582 partitioned into hundreds, tens and ones?
items.e: 582 has 5 hundreds, 8 tens, 2 ones. Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 500 + 80 + 2.

items.q: How do you write 603 in words?
items.e: 603 is 6 hundreds, 0 tens, 3 ones. Say the hundreds, then “and”, then the tens and ones: six hundred and three. There are 0 tens, so we say nothing for the tens.

items.q: Write six hundred and fifty-one in numerals.
items.e: Six hundred and fifty-one means 6 hundreds, 5 tens, 1 one: 600 + 50 + 1 = 651.

items.q: What number is 5 + 40 + 900?
items.e: The parts are not in order. Find the hundreds first: 900. Then the tens: 40. Then the ones: 5. 900 + 40 + 5 = 945.

items.q: Which shows 360 partitioned into hundreds, tens and ones?
items.e: 360 has 3 hundreds, 6 tens, 0 ones. Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 300 + 60.

items.q: How do you write 716 in words?
items.e: 716 is 7 hundreds, 1 ten, 6 ones. Say the hundreds, then “and”, then the tens and ones: seven hundred and sixteen. 16 is “sixteen”, not “sixty”.

items.q: Write five hundred and eight in numerals.
items.e: Five hundred and eight means 5 hundreds, 0 tens, 8 ones: 500 + 8 = 508. Write 0 in the tens place. 3-digit numbers have only 3 digits, so it is not 5,008.

sets.title: 10 or 100 more or less, and counting in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s

items.q: What is 10 more than 347?
items.e: 10 more than 347: only the tens digit changes. 347 + 10 = 357.

items.q: What is 100 more than 462?
items.e: 100 more than 462: only the hundreds digit changes. 462 + 100 = 562.

items.q: Count in 4s: 20, 24, 28, 32, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before. 32 + 4 = 36.

items.q: Count in 50s: 150, 200, 250, 300, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 more than the one before. 300 + 50 = 350.

items.q: What is 10 less than 586?
items.e: 10 less than 586: only the tens digit changes. 586 − 10 = 576.

items.q: What is 100 less than 618?
items.e: 100 less than 618: only the hundreds digit changes. 618 − 100 = 518.

items.q: Count in 8s: 24, 32, 40, 48, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 8 more than the one before. 48 + 8 = 56.

items.q: Count in 100s: 340, 440, 540, 640, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more than the one before. 640 + 100 = 740. Only the hundreds digit changes.

items.q: Which number would you say when counting in 4s from 0?
items.e: 7 × 4 = 28, so you say 28 when counting in 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28. 26, 18 and 34 are in the 2 times table, but not the 4 times table.

items.q: What is 10 more than 295?
items.e: 10 more than 295: change the tens digit. 295 + 10 = 305. 9 tens and 1 more ten make 10 tens = 1 hundred, so the hundreds digit goes up too.

items.q: Count in 4s: 12, 16, ☐, 24, 28. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The numbers go up by 4 each time. 16 + 4 = 20. Check: 20 + 4 = 24.

items.q: What is 10 less than 503?
items.e: 10 less than 503: change the tens digit. 503 − 10 = 493. There are 0 tens, so take 1 ten from the hundreds: 5 hundreds → 4 hundreds and 9 tens.

items.q: Count back in 50s: 500, 450, 400, 350, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 less than the one before. 350 − 50 = 300.

items.q: Which number would you say when counting in 8s from 0?
items.e: 8 × 8 = 64. 68 is in the 4 times table but not the 8 times table. 54 and 58 end in 4 and 8 but are not multiples of 8.

items.q: What is 100 less than 140?
items.e: 100 less than 140: change the hundreds digit. 140 − 100 = 40. 1 hundred take away 1 hundred leaves 0 hundreds, so the answer has only 2 digits.

items.q: Count in 8s: 40, 48, ☐, 64, 72. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The numbers go up by 8 each time. 48 + 8 = 56. Check: 56 + 8 = 64.

items.q: 10 more than a number is 400. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. The number is 10 less than 400. 400 − 10 = 390. Check: 390 + 10 = 400.

items.q: What is 100 more than 900?
items.e: 100 more than 900: change the hundreds digit. 900 + 100 = 1,000. 9 hundreds and 1 more hundred make 10 hundreds = 1 thousand.

items.q: Count back in 100s: 920, 820, 720, 620, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 less than the one before. 620 − 100 = 520. Only the hundreds digit changes.

items.q: Which number would you say when counting in 50s from 0?
items.e: Counting in 50s always ends in 00 or 50: 550, 600, 650, 700. 605, 520 and 675 do not end in 00 or 50.

sets.title: Compare, order and estimate numbers to 1,000

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens: 5 tens is more than 2 tens. So 352 > 325.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. Start with the hundreds: 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds. So 501 > 419. Do not look at the last digit first: 9 ones is less than 1 hundred.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens: 4 tens is more than 2 tens. So 742 > 724. 742 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens: 6 tens is more than 5 tens. So 365 > 356. 356 is the smallest.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1,000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 100. Count the marks from 0: 100, 200, 300. The arrow shows 300.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 120 has 3 digits and 99 has only 2, so 120 is greater. Big digits (9 and 9) do not matter when there are fewer digits.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens: 1 ten is more than 0 tens. So 110 > 101. 110 is the greatest. 99 has big digits, but it has only 2 digits, so it is the smallest.

items.q: Put 504, 450, 540 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 450 < 504 (hundreds: 4 < 5). 504 < 540 (tens: 0 < 4). So the order is 450, 504, 540.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1,000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 100. Count the marks from 0: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700. The arrow shows 700.

items.q: Which number is between 450 and 500?
items.e: A number between 450 and 500 is greater than 450 and less than 500. 486 > 450 and 486 < 500, so 486 is between them.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens: 8 tens is more than 0 tens. So 780 > 708. 708 is the smallest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens: 5 tens is more than 3 tens. So 753 > 735.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 400 to 500 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 10, not 1. The arrow is 3 marks after 400: 400 + 30 = 430.

items.q: Put 263, 326, 236 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 236 < 263 (tens: 3 < 6). 263 < 326 (hundreds: 2 < 3). So the order is 236, 263, 326.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens: 6 tens is more than 0 tens. So 860 > 806. 860 is the greatest.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: Each mark is 100. The arrow is halfway between 800 and 900. Halfway between them is 850.

items.q: Which number is between 700 and 800?
items.e: A number between 700 and 800 is greater than 700 and less than 800. 790 > 700 and 790 < 800, so 790 is between them.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 700 to 800 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 10, not 1. The arrow is 6 marks after 700: 700 + 60 = 760.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens: 9 tens is more than 8 tens. So 398 > 389. 389 is the smallest. Do not compare the last digits: 401 ends in 1, but it has 4 hundreds.

items.q: Put 718, 178, 781 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 178 < 718 (hundreds: 1 < 7). 718 < 781 (tens: 1 < 8). So the order is 781, 718, 178.

items.q: George's book has three hundred and eight pages. How do you write this number in numerals?
items.e: Three hundred and eight is 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones. Write 0 in the tens place: 308.

items.q: Four classes collected bottle tops for recycling. Class 3A: 506; Class 3B: 560; Class 3C: 650; Class 3D: 605. Which class collected the fewest?
items.e: Compare the hundreds: 506 and 560 have 5 hundreds. Then the tens: 0 tens < 6 tens, so 506 is the smallest. Class 3A collected the fewest.

items.q: Leo scores 380 points in a game. Kai scores 100 points fewer. How many points does Kai score?
items.e: 100 fewer: only the hundreds digit changes. 3 hundreds → 2 hundreds. 380 − 100 = 280.

items.q: A train has 8 carriages. Each carriage has 50 seats. How many seats are there?
items.e: Count in 50s eight times: 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400. There are 400 seats.

items.q: Use the digits 7, 2 and 5 once each. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the hundreds place, then the next biggest: 7, 5, 2. The greatest number is 752.

items.q: Use the digits 0, 4 and 9 once each. What is the smallest 3-digit number you can make?
items.e: 0 cannot go in the hundreds place, or it would be a 2-digit number. Use the next smallest digit, 4. Then put 0 in the tens and 9 in the ones: 409.

items.q: There are 310 chairs in the school hall. 10 chairs are taken away to be mended. How many chairs are left?
items.e: 10 less: 1 ten → 0 tens. 310 − 10 = 300. The hundreds stay the same.

items.q: A spider has 8 legs. How many legs do 6 spiders have?
items.e: Count in 8s six times: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48. 6 × 8 = 48 legs.

items.q: There are 486 children at Oak Tree Primary School. What is the value of the 8 in 486?
items.e: The 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens = 80.

items.q: Isla counts in 4s from 0: 4, 8, 12, … What is the 10th number she says?
Each table in the classroom has 4 chairs. There are 9 tables. How many chairs are there?
items.e: Count in 4s nine times: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36. 9 × 4 = 36 chairs.

items.q: A farmer has 832 sheep. She sells 100 of them. How many sheep are left?
items.e: 100 less: only the hundreds digit changes. 8 hundreds → 7 hundreds. 832 − 100 = 732.

items.q: The school kitchen cooked 245 school dinners on Monday. On Tuesday it cooked 10 more. How many dinners did it cook on Tuesday?
items.e: 10 more: only the tens digit changes. 4 tens → 5 tens. 245 + 10 = 255.

items.q: Pencils come in boxes of 100. The school has 7 full boxes and 5 more pencils. How many pencils is that?
items.e: 7 boxes of 100 = 700. Add 5: 700 + 5 = 705. There are 0 tens, so write 0 in the tens place.

items.q: Four children counted the pages they read this term. Alfie: 389; Maya: 398; Amelia: 419; Evie: 401. Who read the most pages?
items.e: Compare the hundreds first. 419 and 401 have 4 hundreds; 389 and 398 have only 3. Then the tens: 1 ten > 0 tens, so 419 is the greatest. Amelia read the most. Do not just look at the last digit.

items.q: A sponsored walk is 1,000 m long. The arrow shows where Zara is. How far has she walked?
items.e: Each mark is 100 m. The arrow is 1 mark after 500: 500 + 100 = 600 m.

items.q: The school library has 590 books. It buys 10 new books. How many books does it have now?
items.e: 9 tens + 1 ten = 10 tens = 1 hundred. So 5 hundreds become 6 hundreds and there are 0 tens: 590 + 10 = 600.

items.q: Stickers come in packs of 100, strips of 10 and single stickers. Grace has 4 packs, 6 strips and 3 single stickers. How many stickers does she have?
Raffle tickets for the school fair come in books of 100. Poppy sells 6 books. How many tickets does she sell?
items.e: Count in 100s six times: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600. Poppy sells 600 tickets.

items.q: Ava thinks of a number. It has 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones. What is her number?
items.e: Write the digits in order: 5 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones → 509. The 0 keeps the 5 in the hundreds place.
